column3: NASB follows the critical text with “God said” and “your father and mother” without “your” repeated; the quotations are in capitals.
NASB recasts “a gift” as “has been given to God.”
NASB follows the critical text with “the word of God” (Textus Receptus: “commandment”); it supplies “by this.”
NASB follows the critical text; “draws near to Me with their mouth and” is from the Textus Receptus.
NASB adds “but”; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text with “the disciples” (no “His”).
NASB names “Jesus,” a Textus Receptus word.
“Is cast out into the sewer” is rendered “is eliminated.”
“The perishing sheep” is rendered “the lost sheep.”
“Was worshiping” is rendered “began to bow down before.”
NASB omits “answering”; “from that hour” is rendered “at once.”
NASB has “His feet,” without “Jesus,” like the critical text, and renders “placed” as “laid … down.”
